units_identified: tf2_ros (TransformListener / MessageFilter library, calling BufferCore from a second thread)
E2.evidence: Step 1: the two units whose calls collided are the tf2 library (BufferCore) and the tf2_ros library, whose TransformListener dedicated thread calls BufferCore::setTransform while the application thread calls BufferCore::addTransformableRequest through tf2_ros::MessageFilter::add (both paths reach getLatestCommonTime); the reporter's own node (velodyne_localizer, no public repository) hosts both. Step 2: the crash is in tf2's own logic. BufferCore::getLatestCommonTime, a const method on an object documented as thread-safe (tfoote: 'The tf buffer is supposed to be thread safe.'), used the member 'mutable std::vector<P_TimeAndFrameID> lct_cache_;' declared in tf2/include/tf2/buffer_core.h ('lct_cache_.clear();' then 'lct_cache_.push_back(latest);') without holding a lock, so two concurrent callers corrupt one vector. Any correct peer that calls the buffer from two threads, which the API permits and tf2_ros does by design, triggers it; no value, frame, name, definition, or timing crossing the boundary is wrong. The fix ('-  mutable std::vector<P_TimeAndFrameID> lct_cache_;' / '+  std::vector<P_TimeAndFrameID> lct_cache;' local to the function) changes no declared or referenced interface of either unit.

ineligible_reason: E2 step 2 (internal): the defect is an unprotected mutable member vector (lct_cache_) inside tf2::BufferCore::getLatestCommonTime, a method of an object that the maintainer states 'is supposed to be thread safe'; it corrupts memory whenever two threads call the buffer concurrently, regardless of any assumption between the caller and the library, and the fix (a stack-local vector) changes no interface. The ROBUST record itself classifies it as 'CWE-414: Missing Lock Check' in package tf2, and the crash in issue #92 was not shown resolved by this change.
